text.p: These are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Wednesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's power company Elektroprivreda and the Norwegian division of Siemens signed on Tuesday a contract worth 5.5 million German marks ($3 million) for the reconstruction of Sarajevo's power distribution system.
- Deputy director of Unis-Holding, Muhamed Lemes, signed on Wednesday a letter of intent with a consortium of Malaysian companies on production and disposal of container equipment.

- Spokesman for the office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in Sarajevo, Kris Janowski, said the return of recently re-expelled Moslem refugees to the town of Jajce is expected to start by the end of the week.
- The opposition Joint List protested over "a single- nationality and single-party" composition of a special commission which is supposed to investigate possible misuse of international aid.
- Kasim Omicevic, member of the central bank's main board, said the banknotes of the convertible mark will be issued in three months at the latest.
- Agricultural expert Vjekoslav Selak says Bosnia does not have a strategy of development for agriculture due to a lack of single market and single price policy.
- The Bosnian Journalist Union protested over the British Embassy's charging fees for press coverage and transport during the recent visit of British Princess Diana.

- Federation minister for refugees and social policy, Rasim Kadic, says more than 60,000 refugees returned to Bosnia in the last seven months mostly from Germany, while another 40,000 are expected to return by the end of the year.
- There are 208 radio and television stations in Bosnia, media monitoring organisation, Media plan, reported. --Sarajevo Newsroom, +387-71-663-864
